en: Chan Master Yǎnxī occupied eight seats of enlightenment, and students flocked to him like water rushing into a valley.
The sayings he preserved have been transmitted throughout all quarters; first, not a single word is derivative, and second, not a single phrase is redundant.
The third completely blocks all pathways for intellectual views and reasoning; the fourth cuts off the thicket of complications and habitual traps.
These four points alone sweep away all the corruptions and maladies of the Dharma-gate in recent times; it is no wonder they stand out as preeminent in their era.

Because of this, I understand that Yanxi’s lifelong "teaching of non-teaching" is such that students who read it must do so with a "hearing of non-hearing. This is what is meant by the "single [transmission]."
Selling nothing but the head of a dead cat; those who eat it find cold sweat flowing over their entire bodies. Its efficacy truly does not fall short of that of our predecessors.
I am insufficient for such a task, yet I have briefly raised the corner of this volume to record my joy and satisfaction.
In the summer of the first year of the Kaiping era, You Yu of Jinling—a man who had attained the Way—remarked:
"Those who do not speak are not few; those who do speak are not many. Thus he said: "I have nothing hidden from you. How could I delight in disputation?
To consider silence as concealment and speech as disputation is the fault of the blind; it is not the fault of the sun.
Yue Jiu: I have observed Yanxi. In his daily life, he is as tranquil as a drifting cloud and as still as a withered tree.

Yet, when he adjusts his robes and takes his seat, there is a deep, resonant sound that leaves those who possess mouths speechless; when he unrolls his paper and wields his brush, his strokes are so free and grand that those who possess hands shrink back in awe.
Is this not what is meant by "great eloquence appearing like stammering" and "profound concealment appearing like emptiness"?
In this late age of the Dharma, those who are called great venerable masters have not yet escaped the burden of seeking fame and the pursuit of offerings and profit;

their conduct has not transcended the turbid and evil world, so how could their preaching of the Dharma possess spiritual efficacy? Only Yǎnxī forgot his attachment to reputation and gain, regarding them as having a flavor like chewing wax.
Therefore, what flows forth from his breast is each instance sublime and profound. Twenty years hence, these words shall be widely practiced.
Someone asked me, "How do you know this? I replied, "I am one who understands speech."
The Year of Wumou (1258), the Day of the Winter Solstice. Recorded by Tang Han Boji.

Epilogue to the Stele Inscription for the Recorded Sayings of Master Yanxi, Volume One:
The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Fozhi upon His First Residence at Jingci Chan Monastery on Mount Xianying in Qingyuan Prefecture.
Attendant: Like a pearl.
The Master entered the monastery on the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month in the first year of the Shaoding era. Pointing to the triple gate, he said:
"Not falling into the gate of transformation; sweeping away the public proclamation. If one seeks his tracks, an iron snake lies across the path."
The Buddha Hall. The World-Honored One’s samādhi—Kāśyapa did not know it. Kāśyapa’s samādhi—Ānanda did not know it.
Right now, as you prostrate and burn incense, tell me: what kind of samādhi is this? (He lets out a shout.)
When presenting the governor’s decree and issuing the command of Magadha, one relies entirely upon this; when applying the Demon King’s seal, one likewise relies upon this.
What, then, is this very thing? The certificate states: "The official verification is clear."
He picks up the Dharma robe. To hold it up—it cannot be lifted; it is beyond the breadth of a hair or a filament. He shakes it out. It cannot be shaken down;
it is like a mountain or a peak. Aha! He sweeps the corner of the *kāṣāya* across the small pond.

Pointing to the Dharma seat, he said: "The pivot of the present moment points upward; with a sweeping gesture, he strides forth, overturning valleys and toppling peaks—Mount Sumeru and King Lamp cannot tread upon him.
He then ascended the seat and held up the incense, saying: "This single offering of incense is respectfully offered to the present Emperor to pray for the prolongation of his sacred life:
Ten thousand years! Ten thousand years! Ten thousand times ten thousand years! May it be so wished."
The holy grace is all-pervasive, extending throughout the infinite lands and atoms of the ten directions; his sagely wisdom is boundless, surpassing three great *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas.

Next, he holds up the incense and says: "This single offering of incense is respectfully offered for the Chancellor, the Commander-in-Chief, the Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, and all the honored officials of this administration, to increase their years of official salary. Next, he holds up the incense and says: "This incense is as light as a mountain and yet as heavy as—"
From the finest hairs [of its influence], south of the Great River and north of Tiantai—originating here, rooted here—it has come to possess a source, though it lacks fragrance.
It was offered to the former abbot of Jingshan Xingsheng Wanshou Chan Monastery.
A special bestowal upon Chan Master Fuxin and Great Monk Zeweng, to repay the milk of the Dharma. He sat cross-legged and said:

"When patch-robed monks meet, even 'cracking' and 'pecking' are still at odds. When men of realization encounter one another, they grasp their whips and turn their heads back. Is there anyone here who cannot bear this?"
He sent forth a question. A monk came forward and asked, "When the Buddhas appear in the world, they preach the Dharma to deliver sentient beings.

When you, Master, appear in the world, what skillful means do you employ? The Master said, "Those who recognize their debt of gratitude are few. The monk said, "If that is so, then I shall grind my bones and shatter my body [to repay it]."

The Master said, "Do not be dull-witted. The monk asked, "As for Sanxing’s saying, 'Whenever I meet someone, I come forth; once I have come forth, I do not act for others'—what is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "It cuts through nails and severs iron. The monk asked, "Since he has come forth, why does he not act for others?"
The Master said, "It is fortunate that you, a Zen guest, have this one question. The monk said, "Xinghua said: 'When meeting people, do not go out;
when going out, act for others. The Master said, "Cutting through iron, chopping through nails. The monk said, "Since he meets people, why does he not go out?
The Master said, "I must answer this question for you. The monk said, "Right now, as on this very day, how would the Master [act]?"
"What is a person? The Master said, "Have you even received the blow yet? The monk said, "A sharp sword sweeps away [obstacles] and heaven and earth are still;
a frosty blade is raised and the Dipper and Ox are cold. He then bowed. The Master then said, "Where wisdom does not reach, when the Way is spoken of, horns grow.
The intent is right before one's eyes, yet it is not something reached by the ears or eyes. To let this one move pass, one sits and cuts off the ten voids. [He] rolled up [the scroll].
He unfolds the heaven and earth beyond the mundane; he hangs the sun and moon across the realm. Fully killing and fully giving life, there is releasing and there is gathering.
At such a time as this, have you yet been able to grasp the matters that transcend the world?
"Habitually passing before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion, hand in golden whip, celebrating peace. (The expression of gratitude is not recorded.)
Again, he raised the case: Master Baogong sent someone to deliver a message to Chan Master Sida, saying, "Why do you not go down the mountain to teach and transform sentient beings?
Why do you merely gaze at the clouds and the Milky Way? Sida replied, "The Buddhas of the three periods of time have been swallowed by me in a single gulp;
where else could there be any sentient beings left to teach and transform? The Master said, "Sida has but a single backbone."
The beam was as hard as iron; yet, with a single light tug from a grass rope, it was toppled over. To this day, it remains submerged within the thicket of weeds, appearing and disappearing.

That evening, he gave a small lecture (xiaocan): "If Śākyamuni had not appeared in the world, the scale would have no weights. If Bodhidharma had not come from the West, the ruler would have no markings."
There is a place that is steep and towering, yet where it is steep and towering, it is level and flat; where it is level and flat, it is steep and towering. Holding up his staff, he said:
"When lifted up, the earth turns and heaven revolves; when set down, the wind blows and the grass bows. When it is neither like this nor that, what then?
Leaning on his staff, he said: "My home is in the Eastern Province. He then cited the case of Master Yaoshan, who gave a small-scale sermon (xiaocan) for the assembly, saying:
"There is one phrase. I will tell it to you when the *te* ox gives birth to a calf. At that time, a monk came forward and said, "The *te* ox has given birth to a calf;
please, Master, speak it! Yaoshan said, "Bring me some fire. The monk withdrew and returned to the assembly. The Master said:
Yaoshan poked his head out too far; he was as if oblivious to those around him. This monk possessed keen and penetrating vision, acting in accordance with the situation.
Even if this were but a single phrase, there would still be a lack of realization remaining.
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "If you try to deliberate upon this with even a single phrase, I, Jingci, cannot deceive you.
If you do not deliberate upon this with a single phrase, you cannot deceive me, Jingci. With a sharp strike, he said: "The matter is reached and the principle is reached;
heaven is level and earth is level. Why, then, is the Main Peak high and the Foreground Peak low?"
Ascending the hall: The pupils in the eyes of Yangqi; the marrow in the crown of Linji’s head. One is not it; two are not it.
If you do not respond when pointed out, white clouds stretch for ten thousand miles.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "A thousand fathoms of sheer cliff—dangerous! He struck the left side of the meditation seat and said, "Venerable Nan-yuan, go over to this side.
"The spark of flint and the flash of lightning are dull! He struck the right side of the meditation seat and said, "Master Linji, go over to that side.

"The Mahāyāna Dharma is beyond the four propositions and transcends the hundred negations. He let out a shout. "The three sections are not the same; they are all gathered back into the previous category."
On the occasion of the Mid-Autumn Festival, former acquaintances ascended to the hall. If one were to discuss this matter, it is like the moon on the fifteenth night;
yet this is still merely lingering before one's eyes—a radiance that has not yet penetrated through. It must be directly beneath the crown of the head, where the heavens and earth are pitch black.
Nevertheless, within the school of the patch-robed monks, there is a place for mutual recognition. Why is this so? Because I am a man of the mountains who loves [the mountain life].

He spoke of matters concerning the mountains. He ascended the hall and said: "The myriad phenomena of the universe are all sealed by a single Dharma. By day one sees the sun; by night one sees the stars.
The pine is naturally straight; the thorn is naturally crooked. What is this single Dharma? "One winter, two winters. He crossed his hands at his chest.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "When Deshan entered the gate, he would strike immediately—like chewing on the sweet tip of a sugarcane.

When Linji entered the gate, he would shout immediately—like a hungry man whose mind is frantic. Holding up his staff, he said: "The very lives of these two great elders now fall into the hands of Jingci.
If I do not let them pass, the entire world will shatter like ice melting away. He leaned on the staff and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "As when a Buddha sees a Buddha, there is no different seeing; as when the Dharma preaches the Dharma, there is no different preaching.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva took money to buy a sesame cake—why, upon letting go of his hand, did he find it was actually a steamed bun? He gave a shout.
Upon ascending the hall for the occasion of the exemption from tomb-related duties, the Master raised the ancient worthy’s saying: "This matter is like a single plot of land;
its four boundaries and the title deeds are all clearly defined, and everything has been handed over to the various people at once.
Only the central tree still belongs to this old monk. The Master said: "The ancients had only the intention to accept the jade tablet, yet they lacked the resolve to cut through the city walls."

How could one know that this temple belongs to the Imperial Court, and that these monks are monks of the Song lands? Within the impartial transformation of the King’s governance, the fine mountains remain as green as ever.
When the Buddha attained enlightenment, he ascended the hall—mistake, mistake! For six years, one was bound in vain by grass ropes. Now, having opened the eyes, it is clear.

The sky breaks into great dawn. The heavens and earth of past and present; the sun and moon of past and present; the stars and constellations of past and present. [He] strikes his knee and says: "The sword has long since departed;
one must strictly avoid marking the boat."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Speech is slander; silence is deception. Beyond both speech and silence, there is a matter that remains.
I, Jingci, shall explain it through for you directly. If you can understand, the Yellow River will flow backward to the north. If you do not understand, the grass south of the city will turn yellow."
The Bathing of the Buddha: Entering the Hall. Rolled over from the belly of a horse and the womb of a donkey; His entire body and face are covered in dust and grime.
In vain do you offer scented water to wash him year after year. If there is anyone who can provide the final phrase, I grant that you have personally seen the Old Man Śākyamuni.
A Small Sermon for the Summer Retreat: Even for one who is non-active and without affairs, there remains the difficulty of the golden chain;

how much more so for those who establish liberation and bondage, or establish cultivation and realization? Within that which has no tracks, they instead create tracks; within that which has no calculation, they instead create calculations.
This is very much like gouging a sore on healthy flesh or adding shackles to a neck already bound by a yoke;
how can one avoid this fault? If you do not enter the water, how will you see the tall man? Again, it is said: Master Yaoshan did not ascend the hall for a long time.

The administrators requested him to preach the Dharma for the assembly. Yaoshan said, "Strike the bell. The administrators struck the bell, and the great assembly gathered together. Yaoshan then returned to his quarters.
The Abbot said, "I have granted permission for you to preach the Dharma for the assembly; why then do you not utter a single word? Yaoshan said, "The sutras have masters of the sutras;
the treatises have masters of the treatises. Why should one find fault with this old monk? The Master said, "Silk is not as good as bamboo;
bamboo is not as good as flesh. This belongs to the old man Yaoshan. But what about when he spoke thus at the very end? It was still..."
Hiding half her face with the lute, she becomes even more charming so that others cannot see her.
On the following day, he ascended the hall: "The great has no exterior; the small has no interior. Coming from the south, coming from the north, falling eastward, tumbling westward.
Not seeking the Buddha; not seeking the Dharma. Ninety days within the mountains; thousands of years beyond the clouds."
Ascending the hall to thank the former and new administrators: Jade is tested by fire; gold is tested by stone; water is tested by a staff;

a sword is tested by a hair. At Jingci, it is not so. Only after the snowfall does one know the resilience of the pine and cypress; only when faced with difficulty is the heart of a true man revealed.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "Hearing of the Buddha creates an enemy; awakening to the Way stains one with mud.
If the alms bowl were to become wet twice in a single day, everyone would lack that one essential point. If all were like today, the Old Barbarian would have reason for hope."
When the Daoist ascended the hall, he said: "The Dao gives birth to One; One gives birth to Two; Two gives birth to Three; Three gives birth to the myriad things.
Throughout the entire world, there are ten men and five pairs. If you do not harbor doubt regarding this, consider this:
when Laozi transformed the Hu people into Buddhas, why did he not transform them into Daoists? Ultimately, where does the contradiction lie? From now on, you must strictly avoid mentioning it.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Difficult, difficult! To what extent? Easy, easy! It is right here. Neither difficult nor easy.
One always recalls the second and third months in Jiangnan, when the partridges cry amidst the deep flowers."

Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said, "To understand it in this way is already to be mistaken. He then laid the staff across his lap and asked, "How is it when you do not understand it in this way?
He leaned on the staff and added, "In the end, this would only serve to prolong one's imprisonment and increase one's delusions."
Ascending the hall on the Mid-Autumn Festival: On the fifteenth day of the eighth month, the full moon faces the door; lift up and go forth at once, overturning the manifest proclamation.
Across the vast sky, clouds darken and rain falls in torrents; this single segment of radiant light has no place to rest.
Ascending the hall, he said: "To grasp it together is up to me; to let it go is also up to me. Three times nine is twenty-seven.
Bodhi and nirvana, suchness and liberation. He struck his knee and said: "I have told you clearly, yet you still do not understand.
How much less could you cover it over?"
Ascending the hall for the opening of the furnace: The mind of the ancient Buddhas is right here and now. Holding up his staff and striking it, he says:
"The meditation seat shakes; the brazier shakes. He leans on the staff and asks: "What juice are you looking for inside a fried cake?"

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The nest knows the wind; the burrow knows the rain. A patch-robed monk knows it before it is even raised. Yet, I, Jingci, do not dare grant him my approval. Why?
To trigger the mechanism, one must have a crossbow of a thousand-jun strength."

Ascending the hall on the day of the winter solstice, if one’s preaching of the Dharma does not accord with the occasion, it is entirely untimely speech. On this auspicious day of the long winter solstice, heaven is clear and earth is tranquil.
We humbly pray that the administrative officers will exert their utmost for the sake of the assembly; that the Head Seat and the great multitude will maintain single-minded focus without distraction;

and that each may receive blessings appropriate to the time. Without clinging to old conventions, there shall be celebration in all things. Whether turning left or right, you may take it for certain that [the assembly] will be complete.
Unshared. Ascending the hall: where words cannot reach, every single phrase is a phrase; where action cannot reach, every single step is a step.
When action reaches its limit and speech reaches its limit, one receives the verdict in full. The old toothless barbarian; Pao-t’uo of the Broken Oven at Mount Sung.
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "If you call this a 'staff,' you bury your own spiritual brilliance;
if you do not call it a 'staff,' you辜负 (gu fu) [disappoint] the former sages. He threw down the staff and asked: "Have you not seen what the Great Master Yunmen said?
'The entire Tripitaka of teachings speaks only of this.'"

Ascending the hall on the first day of the year: "The New Year begins with a fresh dawn; I raise an old public case (gong'an). To attempt to fathom it would be irrelevant. The spring colors of an intercalary year come late. Ascending the hall:
"If you wish to see peace and stability, you must overturn the chaos of heaven and earth. If you seek one who truly knows you, you must turn over the mountains and seas."
Jingci’s passing was a moment of leisurely effort; sitting upright, he received offerings, bringing long-lasting peace and happiness to his patrons.

On the second intercalary month, ascending the hall: whether it be a large or small month, an intercalary year occurring once every three years—whether a full or partial presentation, placing eyebrows upon the eyes, there is confusion and no handle to grasp. To let one move past is to fall into the secondary.

Ascending the hall, he said: "From the beginning we have lived together, yet you do not know my name. 'Lacquered bucket! Lacquered bucket! Let us proceed spontaneously and just as we are. I only fear it is not so;
even the sages of antiquity could not recognize it. A leper child drags along his companion—how could ordinary, common folk ever understand?
Fortunately, there is this one phrase."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "From the time of the ancient ancestors down to the present, one person transmits what is empty, while ten thousand people transmit what is real.
This is like striking with the staff or shouting 'Hè'—it cuts through iron and chops through nails, yet it remains nothing but a dripping, sloshing mess. He then held up his whisk and said:
"Why has this thing reached us all the way to this very day?"

Small-scale *Sanchan* for the End of the Summer Retreat: The Buddha-dharma has endured for two thousand years; not even a hair’s breadth has shifted. These ninety days in the mountains have been continuous from beginning to end.

Exhausting the ten directions and three periods of time, reaching the limits of this land and the Western Heaven, there is nothing left unaddressed in any place, yet everything is accomplished in every place.
Why must one travel south in search? In every location, at the eastern boundary of the City of Enlightenment, there is no need to snap one's fingers—the sun, moon, and pavilions are already present.

The gate opens. Within the school of the patch-robed monks (*śramaṇa*), this is not yet the ultimate principle. If you are such a person, you do not fall into the worldly efforts of the age, nor do you traverse the rungs of the Buddhas’ ladder.
After all, how is it? [He] strikes the meditation seat and says: "A single arrowhead pierces the three barriers; clearly visible is the path behind the arrow. Again, he cites:
Master Baling asked a monk, "Have you come from traveling the mountains, or have you come for the sake of the Buddha-dharma?"
The monk approached. Nan-ch'ing said, "In this world of purity and peace, what Dharma do you speak? The monk said, "A fine 'no-matter' Chan practitioner you are.
Nan-ch'ing said, "You have already done too much. The monk said, "I spent last summer here, did I not? Nan-ch'ing said, "You did, Upāsaka."
The monk said, "No. Lingyun said, "If that is so, then we have not known each other since long ago. The monk went down.

The Master said, "Baling may truly be called the gate of Mengchang; this monk is also naturally adept at being a guest—advancing when it is time to advance and withdrawing when it is time to withdraw."

This is truly a matter of host and guest being in perfect harmony. It is just like when Baling said, "If it were so, we would not have known each other from the start"—having gone down [the path], what was his intention?
Three cups of wine to brighten the countenance of a young lord; a single branch of flowers to adorn the head of a beautiful woman.
Ascending the hall: When Mazu ascended the hall, Baizhang rolled up his mat. Jingci looks at this and sees that an inch is not equal to a foot. Ascending the hall:
Yunmen letting Dongshan off with three blows of the staff is like feeding a baby with chewed food; Huangbo giving Linji three blows of the staff is like forcing an ox’s head down to eat grass.
Right now, without violating even a single thread of principle, there is a skillful means. (He remains silent for a long while.)
He said, "The great matter cannot be handled by you; the small matters must be undertaken by yourselves.
On the festival day, he ascended the hall. "The multitude of yin has been stripped away; the single yang returns.
Holding up his staff, he said, "This staff follows local custom and enters into worldly ways. He struck it once and said, "Six times six does not equal thirty-six."
Ascending the hall, he said: "To mention one is to clarify three; to ask ten is to answer a hundred. When the wind stirs the dust or the grass moves, they raise their eyebrows and go forth.
Each and every one of them cannot be deceived by even a single point. Reaching out his hand, he asked: "How is my hand like the Buddha-hand?"

A Small Sermon on New Year’s Eve: When a single speck of dust enters right-reception (*samāpatti*), heaven and earth are silent and still; when all specks of dust arise from samādhi, the world is vast and imposing.
Thus one sees the year end and the age pass, things changing and times shifting. The old Wang of East Village burns paper money at night; Zhang drinks the wine while Li gets drunk.
At this very moment, the great capacity suddenly awakens, and it does not hinder the free circulation of the true eye. It is precisely thus...
"At this time, is there still the meaning of 'the non-transmigration of things' or not?
[The Master] lets out a shout. He then cites an ancient worthy who said: "If I were to tell you, I fear my tongue would be worn away;
if I do not tell you, I fear my mouth would be silenced. Is there still a way to benefit others? The Master says: "I shall speak."
Understood. The commentary has been annotated and understood. Yet, though his intention was to benefit others, it instead ends up deceiving them.
On the first day of the year, he ascends the hall and says: "Last night we sent off the old year; this morning we celebrate the new year.
The infinite Dharma-gates and hundreds of thousands of samādhis—[beating the meditation seat]—are once again starting from the beginning."

Shaking hands with the new and old assembly as they take their places in the hall: the Patriarch’s command is being put into practice; the entire faculty is liberated in its full power. East passes to the west, the west passes to the east.
When released, all are released; when gathered, all are gathered. It is like two horses grappling head-to-head; I, this mountain monk, simply watch.
The Buddha ascended the hall for the occasion of his *parinirvāṇa*. "The Buddhas do not appear in the world; for forty-nine years they have preached. Do not slander Old Śākyamuni!
The Buddhas do not appear in the world, nor is there any *parinirvāṇa*. Do not slander Old Śākyamuni!
If someone asks why today is so extraordinary, do not slander Old Śākyamuni!"
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff, struck it once, and said: "The fruit is full and bodhi is perfected. He struck it again: "The flower blooms and the world arises.
Is this the wondrous functioning of spiritual powers, or is it simply the nature of things as they are? He struck it twice in succession:
"One might think spring has returned to nowhere to be found, yet one does not know it has shifted its place and come here."
Ascending the hall at the beginning of the summer retreat: "All day long it is perfect enlightenment, yet one has never experienced perfect enlightenment. With eyes open, one falls into the bed;
fully possessing perfect enlightenment, one dwells within perfect enlightenment, yet is drowned in stagnant water. Why is this? Within the treasury of our King, there is no such sword."
Xie Dusi ascended the hall for the Summer Retreat. "A single phrase contains all flavors; I bring it forth with full sincerity to offer to you all.
It is not Dongshan’s 'Iron Sour Plum,' nor is it Yangqi’s 'Thorny Chestnut. Looking left and right, he said:
'How does today’s offering compare to yesterday’s?'"
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: A monk once asked Yunmen, “What is the place where all Buddhas emerge?
Yunmen replied, “Water flows uphill on the Eastern Mountain. Later, Master Yuanwu said, “If it were Tianning, it would not be so. What is the place where all Buddhas emerge?
‘A fragrant breeze blows from the south; the halls and pavilions grow cool. The Master said, “If you understand it in this way...”
To go see Yunmen is easy; to see Yuanwu is difficult. If you do not understand it in this way, then to see Yuanwu is easy;
to see Yunmen is difficult. Today, if someone asks, "What is the place where all Buddhas emerge?
simply tell them: "The third and the eleventh; the ninth and the seventh."

Opening the furnace, he ascends the hall: "The teachings of the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the canon are much like describing the taste of food; the separate transmission outside the teachings is truly like a painted cake.
If you wish to be authentic, you must respond to the times like the wind and respond to conditions like lightning; by all means, avoid deliberating in a lukewarm place."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "As soon as there is something valued, it immediately becomes a trap. He struck his staff and said: "I, this mountain monk, simply keep opening it;
you all simply keep cutting it off. For a moment, let us set it down before a dark window; tomorrow, I shall calculate it with you once more."
He leaned on his staff and descended from the seat.
On the first day of the year, he ascended the hall and said: "If there is Buddha-dharma for the New Year, there are forty-nine instances at one stroke.
If there is no Buddha-dharma for the New Year, a gourd hangs on the eastern wall. Today, the heavy gate is once again flung wide open; How much spring scenery fills the rivers and lakes!"
The Buddha ascended the hall for his *nirvāṇa* discourse: "On the eighth day of the fourth month he was born; on the fifteenth day of the second month he entered extinction.
Although birth and extinction are fundamentally empty, this is precisely the moment of the total presentation. Coral branches support the moon, branch after branch."
Recorded by Attendant Ruzhu, compiled at Zhidu Chan Temple on Mount Xiangshan in Qingyuan Prefecture. At the Buddha Hall:
Yunmen’s striking with the staff must not be let pass; at Xiangshan’s prostration, letting it pass is not permitted. From of old...
Offerings to the Buddha do not depend on the abundance of incense.
To occupy the abbot’s quarters and enter the chamber of the Fragrant Mountain requires one who is truly a person of the Fragrant Mountain.
If, before even crossing the threshold, you knit your brows and turn back, I shall strike my knee and say: "I guarantee this matter for you."

That evening’s informal discourse: The Great Way is right before your eyes. To try to clarify or break through it is already inadequate; yet, for now, it is difficult to behold. Not yet there? Speak further!
If you wish to recognize the true substance of the Great Way, you must strictly avoid following in others' footsteps. It does not depart from sound, form, or speech. Indeed!
From the time of the ancestors until now, whether Buddhas or Patriarchs, within that which has no tracks, they have instead created tracks. There are none...

"Releasing [the ox] to the west of the stream, it cannot avoid eating the water and grass belonging to the king. It is better to accept what little one has according to one's lot.

Ascending the hall: At all times, do not give rise to deluded thoughts—just so, just so. Yet, regarding these deluded minds, do not suppress or extinguish them—neither so, nor not so.
Abiding within the realm of delusive thoughts, do not apply analytical knowledge—within suchness, yet it is not so.
Within this lack of analytical knowledge, do not discriminate what is real—not so, yet within that not-so, it is so. *Claps hands.*
The Bed: Without following the path of the woodcutter, how could one reach the home of Ge Hong?
Ascending the hall: Wealth and honor are easy to attain; one might even sever one’s own natural arm amidst the snow. Poverty and want are difficult to endure;
when the mind cannot be found anywhere, where else can it find rest? Difficult, difficult! Last night the wind grew fierce; the solitary traveler was already chilled first.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Under the gate of Xiangyan, there is neither Chan nor Dao; there is only one great Mount Peng.

I would simply say to him: 'It is just so.'"
Master Baofu Jieshi ascended the hall for the morning service. "The final word of Mount Jing: opening one's mouth turns it into a public proclamation.

Leaning on his staff, he descended from the seat.
For the Imperial Festival, he ascended the hall: "The phrase that cannot be uttered even with one's full strength does not lie at Tiantai; it must surely be at Nanyue.
For a thousand years in the mountain forests, he now clearly brings it forth all at once: "The peaks of Huading at Tiantai are exquisite; the Stone Bridge at Nanyue is lofty."
A Small Sermon for the Eve of the New Year: If there were even a single dharma, mountains, rivers, and the great earth would all sink away.

If there were not even a single dharma, the myriad phenomena and the ten thousand forms would shine forth in brilliant clarity. The old year departs this very night; yet as it departs, it truly does not depart. The new year arrives tomorrow;
yet as it arrives, it truly does not arrive. [He strikes the whisk and says: "All are shattered here and now, at once. One dharma...

The myriad dharmas—new year and old year—are entirely encompassed by the Great Earth. In a single stroke, a thousand differences are resolved; there is no coming or going, and no shifting or exchanging.
When shifting occurs, they further interpenetrate; otherwise, they abide according to their respective positions.
Again, he raised this case: A monk asked Zhaozhou, "What is it like when there is a difference as slight as a hair's breadth? Zhaozhou said, "Heaven and earth are separated by vast distances.

He struck the ground three times with the staff, saying, "Heaven and earth harmonize their virtue; the sun and moon harmonize their brightness. This is actually the hexagram *Taitian* (Earth over Heaven). Although...
Thus, the inner trigram has already been clarified; let us further seek the outer image. O staff-bearer, do not follow human sentiment;
do not follow human will. (He strikes the desk three times. What follows is a long discourse: "All will be auspicious and nothing will be disadvantageous."
Ascending the hall for the concluding ceremony of the Imperial Birthday: "Clouds follow the dragon; wind follows the tiger. When the Sage appears, all things behold him.

At that time, when the faculty of thought lingers and hesitates, one cannot avoid missing the path before one's eyes. Do you know where Wanshou has landed?
The flowers must bloom through the night, waiting for the morning breeze to blow.

Again, the case is cited: Once, when Master Fachang was eating fruit with Chief Seat Gan, Fachang picked up a tangerine and said, "How does this flavor compare to that of Huanglong? This is why I say: 'If you can speak thus, you are a true successor; if you cannot speak thus, you are a follower. He further said, "Fachang’s teaching was like a great bell struck once—it resonated throughout the ten directions. Gan’s teaching was like a small bell struck repeatedly—it only reached those nearby. He concluded, "If you can understand this, you will see the difference between the ancient and the modern. If you cannot understand this, you will remain lost in the weeds of words. Thus he spoke.
Fachang lightly cast his fragrant bait, yet the Head Seat caught him on his hook and line.

At that moment, had he picked up the tangerine and immediately withdrawn his body, he would not only have cut off Fachang’s tongue, but would also have manifested the head and horns of the Yellow Dragon.
Ascending the hall on the Winter Solstice: When the sun reaches its southernmost point at the longest day, the primary truth (*paramārtha-satya*) precedes any verbal expression;
what need is there to seek its very core? After all, how is it? A catfish climbing a bamboo pole—ten thousand miles in a single day.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "If you understand when the Buddha had not yet appeared in the world, you are merely looking at the sutras inside a temple.

For what reason, then, is it said that even this is 'not yet'? [What of] Linji’s Three Mysteries and Fushan’s Nine Strands?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "Everyone is driven by the twelve hours of the day, rushing about like a moth to a flame. This old monk, however, makes use of the twelve hours;
when his meal is finished, he plays with his chopsticks. Although Zhaozhou emptied his guts and turned over his belly, heaven has not yet been established—hell was already formed first."
Small Sermon for the Summer Retreat: To clarify only the self while failing to comprehend what is before one’s eyes is to emerge from and submerge into a ghost cave.
If one comprehends what is before one’s eyes yet fails to clarify the self, one merely shuffles feet forward and backward upon level ground, darkly passing through two layers of barriers.
Not traveling the path of the mind, one sweeps away habitual patterns and establishes a distinct livelihood—this is precisely "leaving Zhengzhou to enter Cao’s Gate. Consider this.
This has nothing to do with agitation and sinking; how much less could it involve the arousal of great potential or the manifestation of great function?
It is as lively and agile as a bird’s two wings, revolving and turning like the two wheels of a chariot. When both the knot and its untying are forgotten, the eyes and feet are used together.
This is far more than merely making a living in dead water. If one speaks from the standpoint of the monk’s gate, even eighty thousand miles is not considered far.

Ascending the hall in the Central Kingdom: more than half of the ninety-day summer retreat has passed. As for this ready-made public case, even clear-eyed monks cannot settle it;

Incense Offering for the Memorial of Chan Master Focin: Before thirty years have passed, hearing one’s name is not as good as seeing one’s face;
after thirty years have passed, seeing one’s face is not as good as hearing one’s name. One is not so; two are not so. Burning incense within the bowl.
Purple clouds gather and billow; he lifts up the incense smoke. Do you see it?
His true face is present right now. Opening the brazier, he ascends the hall; not a single wandering monk is in sight. Fachang flaunts his elegance:
the ancient mirror is as wide as the brazier. Xuefeng sets a pattern by providing a model. To examine this closely: when it is hot, it kills with heat; when it is cold, it kills with cold.
Who would have known that within cold ashes, the fragrance of ninefold refinement permeates the bottle?

Do you know where Ten-Thousand-Year Longevity resides? Even the kalpa-stones have a day when they are worn away; empty space has no time of exhaustion.

On the occasion of the imperial birthday, the assembly is convened for this Dharma hall discourse. I tune the melody of Yunmen to manifest the highest faculty; I sing the song of Great Peace to delight in the transformation of non-action.
*He strikes his staff once.* Taking only the intent of a thousand ages, I pour forth my heart at this very moment.

To pierce straight through the skull and replace the eyes, one must be a master of the tide if one wishes to enter the surging waves."
Ascending the hall for the concluding ceremony on the anniversary of the Sage’s birthday: The entire earth is his total capacity, stretching across and hanging within the sun and moon;
the whole world is his wondrous function, rolling up and unfolding beyond the heaven and earth of the phenomenal realm.
At such a time as this, what is the phrase for knowing gratitude and repaying kindness? The Yellow River clears itself but once every three thousand years.

by the shores of Lake Dongting, one does not know that a single sail has already passed. To be thus muddled and ignorant—is there any need to compare such things?
Why is this? "If one were to select a Buddha without such an eye, even a thousand years would be of no avail.

"Why do you not prostrate? As he was about to rise after his prostration, he suddenly attained awakening. The Master said, "Where has the one who received sixty blows from Huangbo gone?

entering the mountains, he returns from the mountains; the iron wall, again the iron wall. Within the school of the patch-robed monks, he strikes the whisk and says:

Only this present day is most auspicious; it manifests excellence within excellence, and auspiciousness within auspiciousness.
May there be a lifespan of ten thousand years and a thousand autumns; may this single incense offering reach the nine heavens.

Why? Because the death [of the Buddha] was in the hands of his disciples—it was no extra burden for him.

If you can act in this very way, you have entered the gate of Yuyang; yet, if you wish to see the man of Yuyang, you must go further and further away.
Try looking at Minggong Xi on the sea—how does he compare to Jian, the Head Seat in the hall?

Ascending the hall: Bodhidharma faced the wall; Yunmen recited the *Saptāha Sūtra*. The jade is naturally without flaw; carving patterns destroys its virtue. Ascending the hall:

Three gates. South of the mountain, the screen-like peaks are high; to the west, the waters of the lake flow swiftly. Do you still hear the sound of the Yan River?

[The Master] reaches the limit of his discourse. Next, he holds up the incense and says:

may their majesty awe the barbarians, restoring the territories to the ancient lands of the Three Rivers. [Next, he picks up the incense.]

[The Master] says: "This single offering of incense is respectfully offered for the Chancellor, Pacifier of the Borderlands, Grand Councilor, Director of the Department of Transportation, Palace Supervisor, and Minister of the Left.

Neither establishing nor clearing away, with fresh and pure compassion: where there is water, one travels by boat; where there is no water, one walks on foot.
Borrowing a path to pass through, he enters the city of Rājagṛha. Clouds rise over the southern mountains while rain falls upon the northern mountains.

The Buddha-Dharma has no fear of being soaked or ruined. Why? "The clouds of the nine heavens have stilled, and the boundaries are vast; the royal way is impartial, so one may walk with arms swinging free. (The expression of thanks is not recorded. Again, he raised [the case]:
Emperor Taizong of the Great Song dynasty was once visited by a monk from Woyun Hermitage who came for an audience. The Emperor asked, "In the depths of Woyun, one does not face the imperial court;
why have you come here? The monk was speechless. Xuedou Mingjue spoke on his behalf, saying, "It is difficult to escape the ultimate transformation.
The Master said: "Heaven opens and earth spreads; the sun shines and the moon descends. This monk met [the Emperor] yet did not meet him; he drew the sword [in vain]."

That evening, during the informal discourse: "The waters return to the vast ocean; ten thousand streams flow toward the source. The moon reaches the center of the sky;
there is no hidden place it does not illuminate. This is like the place where a patch-robed monk walks, like the place where a patch-robed monk acts.

Where light meets, darkness meets; let everything be cast entirely into the radiance of the Mirror of the Source. At that moment, Leifeng Pagoda and Huiriguo Hall converse face-to-face, unaware and unperceived.
"Understood. At the single flash of the mirror's light, arguments arose like sharp blades: unifying the many into one, and unifying the one into the many.
He realized that this was the intent of the Patriarchs and the intent of the Teachings; yet within this light, he could not resolve the distinctions between them.

This led Yongming to be unable to restrain his impatience, and he analyzed and adjudicated the essential subtleties of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. These are not to be sought through competitive debate; a new official [cannot grasp them].
To settle this old matter, the text below is long; I entrust it to a future day. Again, he raised the case:
Huangbo said, "Since Master Bodhidharma arrived in China, he has spoken only of the One Mind and transmitted only the One Buddha. He transmitted Buddha through Buddha, not speaking of other Buddhas;
he transmitted Dharma through Dharma, not speaking of other Dharmas. Dharma is the ineffable Dharma; Buddha is the [ineffable] Buddha."
"To take it as the Buddha" refers precisely to the fundamentally pure mind. The Master said: "Huangbo is a master of the Way;
why does he hold the views of a mere Dharma teacher? The Dharma cannot be expounded, and the Buddha cannot be grasped.
If one truly takes this to be the ultimate standard, the entire lineage of Bodhidharma will be swept away."
I thank the new and old assemblies for ascending the hall. You establish the Dharma banner and support the Dharma community; whether moving left or right, you are elegant and refined in your style.
Fully unrolling and fully unfolding like pearls rolling upon a platter, you increase the value of the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye.
The Emperor Huizong’s Memorial Day: Ascending the Hall. Colorful insignia and celestial retinues amidst the five clouds— Behold them simply as they were in the former Emperor’s days.
Do not say that only the bow and sword remain; His majestic wind is so stern it chills the bones.

In the central hall, celebrating the precious canopy, he offered prayers for the Emperor’s long reign. "The wind moves, the banner moves; it is neither the wind nor the banner that moves—it is the mind of the wise man that moves.

With these words, he returned to the source, and the ten thousand nations came to court. "The wind rings, the bell rings; it is neither the wind nor the bell that rings—it is your own mind that rings.
As the six giant turtles pull the mountain, the three peaks rise up. He opens wide the true eye at the crown of the head and brings forth the great function of the ultimate path.
Soaring in the present and shining through antiquity, it is utterly free from obstruction. Pervading the earth and filling the heavens, there is no room for evasion.

Each and every thing interlaces like the Flower Treasury World; layer upon layer, inexhaustible, like the pearls of Indra’s net. The meaning lies right before one’s eyes; it is like adding flowers to brocade.
Several hundred monastics join their voices in celebration; the Venerable Banzhian stirs the earth and radiates light, manifesting abundance and longevity at every turn.
Man. Every object is suffused with the harmonious breath of spring; this may be called a marvelous thing shown within marvel, a supreme cause revealed within supremacy.
At such a time as this, what is the single phrase for repaying kindness? "The Emperor’s power weighs as heavily as a mountain."
"The Emperor's grace is as vast as the universe. He then spoke a verse, saying: "The Buddha’s vast Flower Treasury Ocean, The Dharma and its practice are established therein.
Upon this lion throne of precious flowers, A jeweled canopy hangs down from the heavens.
In ancient times, the son of the Elder Ratnākara Held this canopy in his hands to offer to the Buddha. By the Buddha’s wisdom and majestic spiritual power," [one...]
The single precious canopy merged into one. The Southern Mountain was but a foot and five inches from heaven. The royal city was no different from the city of Vaiśālī.
The mind of that time is the very mind of this time; by means of these adornments, the work of a Buddha is performed.

Colorful banners and jeweled pennants, variegated with gold and azure, appear as layers of light when viewed. It is like a gentle breeze blowing away withered flowers, while fresh ones rain down once more.
Excellent! Looking upward, one observes that the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world-system is entirely filled within this canopy;
as it is with each individual world, so it is with every path, every trail, and every needle’s eye—there is no place where it is not so. How could it be limited to one Buddha or two Buddhas?

Buddhas from throughout the ten directions all appear therein, their broad and long tongues blazing forth as they preach. Of the myriad dharmas and the single dharma, there is none to which they do not pervade. *Huang* (The Imperial)
The sovereign’s mind is in communion with the Buddha-mind; the Emperor’s longevity shall equal that of the Southern Mountain.
I owe this grace and this protection; my heart is like this very mountain.
Ascending the hall: Today is as hot as yesterday. Each of you should take care of yourselves. Ascending the hall on the Mid-Autumn Festival:
This is precisely the time for cultivation. Holding up the moon before the eaves is precisely the way to make offerings. Reaching for the moon in the water—[is this not the very act of cultivation?]
He brushed his sleeves and departed; he brandished his staff and struck the moon. One is three, and three is one.
The colt tramples everyone underfoot; how can the rabbit escape its burrow?
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "A plot of vacant land before the mountain—having thought it forgotten, one joins the palms and earnestly asks the patriarch:
'Are you not a great man? How many times have you sold it only to buy it back? Who wrote this deed?
'Out of love for the pines and bamboo, they draw in the pure wind. Striking the meditation seat with his whisk: "The interests of the noble man are moved."
Ascending the hall: The meaning of the Tathāgata’s Chan and the Patriarchs’ intent is that "one is not established and two are not right.

If you can, right now, press through to the point where you can turn your body and release your breath, why wait until the summit of Mount Ao or before the temple of the Ancient Buddha for your mind to suddenly awaken?

Ascending the hall: At the crossroads stands a stone pillar; there is no place for you to shield yourself. When the cry sounds, "The Minister comes upon the river," there is no place for you to evade it.
You monks, going out in the morning and returning in the evening, stepping here and there—here too you must be careful.
Should you suddenly strike against or bump into something, my staff at Jingci will have another way of dealing with you.

Ascending the hall: Six years of sitting in cold stillness; nine years facing the wall. The pestle pounds toward the southeast; the millstone grinds toward the northwest. On this occasion of the Imperial Birthday, ascending the hall:
the wind does not rustle the branches; the rain does not break the clods of earth. In every atom and every world-system, all is fully revealed—this is entirely the realm of the Great Man.
The North Star shines high above the Southern Mountains.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Zen is not a matter of conceptual thought; the Way transcends all achievement and merit. To depart from these two paths is like the era of Great Peace:
riding a light carriage on a familiar road, there is nowhere one cannot go. Yet, to hope for this under the gates of Deshan or Linji is far removed indeed."
Why is this? Before the painting was made, the *I Ching* already existed; after the [Confucian] canon was edited, the *Shi Jing* no longer exists.
At the summer retreat’s small *chan* (meditation) assembly: if you understand, all things are of one family; if you do not understand, there are ten thousand distinctions and a thousand differences.

To be identical with heaven while being heaven, and to dwell among humans while being human—consider the source: that which can be both heaven and human, how could it be something that heaven and humans are capable of? —Zhaoming.
"Master of the Dharma, your Way is far too severe; it achieves but eighty percent. When the benevolent see it, they call it benevolence; when the wise see it, they call it wisdom.
The common people use it daily yet remain unaware of it; therefore, the Way of the superior man is rare indeed.
The former scholars seem to have grasped it, yet they still fall short by half. I, Nanshan, have never uttered a falsehood from the beginning; wherever I go, I rely on the nine...
Ten days constitute one summer. He has never, even for so much as a single hair’s breadth, erred regarding any person.
If you can understand this, when the drum is beaten in Pūrvavideha, you will be ascending the hall in Aparagoyānī. If it is not yet so, there is porridge and rice upon the long benches.
Again, he raised an example: A monk asked Caoshan, "The monk Qing is destitute; I beg the Master to provide relief. Caoshan said:
He summoned Dharma Master Shui. Shui responded with a "Yes. Caoshan said, "Qingyuan Bai drank three cups of wine, yet he still says he has not even touched his lips.
The Master said, "Dharma Master Shui, you employ the art of the shadow-body; old Caoshan employs the mechanism of binding the tiger.
Nevertheless, tell me, where is the place where he drinks the wine?"
The next day he ascended the hall. "People have north and south, but the Way has neither north nor south. From the high seat to the middle and low seats, space is completely filled.

Among them, perhaps one person or half a person is willing to go; what need is there to speak of welcoming them with gruel? To prepare fragrant rice separately in another steamer at Nanshan is not considered an extraordinary thing."
Ascending the hall, he called to the assembly: "This Dharma cannot be understood through thought or discrimination.
To have spent twenty-one days contemplating this matter—how unmanly! To have traveled ten thousand li across the vast ocean only to mislead future generations.
You people here, who come from your private quarters and go into the Sangha Hall as if tigers had sprouted wings, yet you still come here!"
With eyes blinking, what is he lacking?

He hangs the imperial calligraphy of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* and the plaque for the Hall of Universal Knowledge (*Samantabhadra-jñāna*). With great capacity and perfect response, he possesses universal knowledge.
The Great Function manifests before us; lift it upward. Within the sleeves, the divine blade has not yet moved, yet its patterns and brilliance are fully displayed before our eyes.
It opens wide the wondrous gates of hundreds of thousands of samādhis, never falling into the calligraphic styles of the twenty-four masters.
Coming from the Golden Hall, it loftily hangs the light of sun and moon; reflecting upon the White Jade Brow, it further enhances the splendor of the lakes and mountains. This very thing—
The Dharma-realm of the Avataṃsaka—how does it differ from the jeweled pavilion? A single drop of ink becomes a dragon in two places;
events of two thousand years are all realized this very day. But what are the events of this day? "Ten thousand years of imperial reign!"

Ascending the hall on the Double Fifth Festival, the Master wrote talismans of the Duke Wang and employed the ordinances of Shangjun. Ghosts were many and spirits were in chaos; medicine was abundant yet illnesses were severe.

Pointing his finger, he ascended the hall and said:
"To establish knowledge within seeing and knowing is the very root of ignorance; to have no seeing within seeing and knowing is itself nirvana.

The jar. The spring grass is emerald; the spring waters are green waves. As I see you off at the southern ford, how can I bear this grief?

Master Yunshan of Mount He addressed the assembly with this letter: "If there is even a single dharma, one is caught within a cage;

It is like water in a cold month; if one intends to seek clouds and mountains from this, how could they be less than ten million miles of white clouds?

On the occasion of ascending the hall on the Mid-Autumn Festival, [the Master said]: "The water is clear and the moon appears; when it moves, the reflection turns with it. When the water is clear but the moon does not appear, he draws a new arrow from Silla behind his back.
Having overturned the water bowl, he departed immediately, falling into a deep pit of liberation. These three great elders were all like those who have closed their eyes.

[He draws a circle with his whisk and says: "Above all, avoid letting your eyes grow dim."

it is to strike west while pointing east, to enter the circle by holding the square. It is essential that all of you know this. He strikes the whisk and says: "A single point is formed."
The dragon is complete in both places; how about you brothers adding ten strokes?

If you say that from the eastern hedge one can see the Southern Mountains, the hawk has already flown past the kingdom of Silla.
A brief consultation on a winter night: striking before the sound, digging out the collar from under the armpit, and holding up what lies beyond the categories.

Striking the lapel with the sleeve—if one does not possess a penetrating function, one cannot avoid falling entirely into the realm of conventional ritualism. Regarding the Way of Zhenjing, Shishuang Puhui said:
"Rest! Cease! Be cold and still! This is called the bliss of the extinction of the Two Vehicles.

The joy of giving. Apart from these three kinds of joy, nothing else constitutes true happiness. The "True and Pure Old Master" (the Buddha) compared himself to others;
yet, in doing so, he not only buried the former sages but also lost his own single eye. Under the gate of Jingci, there is no need for a holeless flute or felt clappers;
we simply sing and respond according to our capacity, valuing only that we receive blessings in accordance with the times. Have you not heard it said: "Eat simple vegetarian food"?
"Drink water; bend the arm and use it as a pillow—happiness is right there within. [The Master] raised another case:
Guishan asked Yangshan, "Mid-winter’s bitter cold is an annual occurrence; as the movement of the sun's shadow shifts, what is the matter?
Yangshan stood before him with his hands folded. Guishan said, "I knew well that you could not answer this question. Xiangyan said, "I, [your disciple],..."
He answered specifically regarding the words of the one who had attained. Guishan followed up on the previous question; Xiangyan also joined his palms and stepped forward to stand near him.
Guishan said, "Fortunately, Jizi did not understand. The Master [Zhaozhou] said, "Yangshan failed to reach the village in front;
Xiangyan failed to overtake the inn in the rear. Do you still know that Guishan was old and solitary in heart?"

Ascending the hall on the Winter Solstice: The sun reaches its southern limit; all is auspicious and nothing is unfavorable. The ice cracks open the clod of earth; flowers bloom upon the pestle’s tip.
Ascending the hall on the eighth day of the twelfth month: Words are sufficient when they exhaust the Way; words are insufficient when they exhaust phenomena.
At the ultimate point of the Way and phenomena, neither speech nor silence is enough to carry them. Yet it is not through non-speech or non-silence that their meaning is found.
These few words—there is no one in all the world who does not know them. Yet, to truly see the Old Man with the Yellow Face is something as vastly different from this as heaven is from earth.
Why? Because the stars are in the heavens, while the wood is on the ground.
On New Year’s Day, the Master ascended the hall. "The entire earth, gathered up, is no larger than a grain of millet;
I cast it before you—strike the drum, everyone, and look! Old Xuefeng, at that time, wrote out a calendar right before people's eyes.
Those of later generations throughout the world know only that night is dark and day is bright; they often miss the matter in between. How shall Nanshan express his gratitude?

Peace and prosperity! Today, all that is within reach of the sun has been brought forth. In the first year of the Baoyu era, during the spring of the sovereign’s reign, ten thousand streams flow toward the ocean and a thousand chariots follow the same track.

Ascending the hall on the occasion of the Emperor’s Birthday: Now, those who preach the Dharma speak in accordance with the Dharma. Incense is offered for the Southern Mountain; may his longevity equal that of the Northern Gate.
Upon the arrival of a letter from Master Dachuang, he ascends the hall: He comes with no fixed place; Dachuang is entirely contained within a single hair.
Departing without fixed location, the sacred traces remain where the monkeys cry. The void bursts open, casually exchanging the eyes of all quarters.
Mountains and rivers dance, shaking the celestial gates and rattling the earth’s portals. O assembly, do you still know the final word from the eastern ravine?
"Each and every samādhi—each and every one does not know. To whom is this meaning clearly spoken?

Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of Master Chuwu. Once, a monk asked him: "Regarding the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings, when one realizes their principle and attains the subtle, are they the same as or different from the meaning of the Patriarchs?
Chuwu said: "One must discern beyond the six phrases; do not allow yourself to be turned by sounds and forms.
The monk asked: "What are the six phrases? Chuwu said: "The spoken, the silent, and that which is neither spoken nor silent."
"It is always not so. How do you act now? The monk was speechless. The Master said, "This monk had a fine question, yet he failed at the end—like a dragon's head with a snake's tail.
To discern the wind from its subtle stirrings, one must fall neither behind the words nor before the sound.
Examining it thus, there is nothing lacking in the school of teaching through doctrine; but as for the gate of the Patriarchs, it is still very far away."
Xie Liangban ascends the hall. With a single shout, host and guest are distinguished; illumination and function proceed simultaneously. He lets out a shout: "There is the guest, there is the host;
there is illumination, there is function. When the dragon gains the water, his spirit increases; when the tiger encounters the mountain scenery, its fierce majesty grows."
Ascending the hall, he said: "To study and learn is called 'hearing'; this is the talkative old master. To cease learning is called 'neighboring'; this is your own way of seeing.
To go beyond these two is what constitutes true transcendence. This may be so, yet you have not escaped being caught in the same arrow or drowning in the same mire.
Why? Vipaśyin Buddha set his mind on it long ago, yet until this very day he has not attained the wondrous."

A Small General Talk for the End of the Summer Retreat. As soon as there is anything held as significant, one has already fallen into a habitual trap. [The Master] strikes the meditation seat and says:

"Whether long-term or short-term retreats, it is like planting trees while gazing at the clouds. Whether studying the conventional or the profound, it is like climbing a tree to catch fish. This causes one to peer over the fence but fail to enter, or to stand by the tripod but not taste its contents.
